source.title: Trainable Dynamic Mask Sparse Attention
source.authors: Jingze Shi; Yifan Wu; Yiran Peng; Bingheng Wu; Liangdong Wang; Guang Liu; Yuyu Luo

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports a perplexity sweep across model sizes for attention variants, but does not fit the original power-law scaling relationships or test compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: Section 5.2 and Figure 5 report a scaling-perplexity comparison on SmolLMCorpus. Downstream benchmark, associative-recall, and needle-in-a-haystack results are not rows because they do not test whether performance is predictably related to scale or pretraining loss. Training configurations are not outcomes.
record.test_reason: The scaling-perplexity sweep (80M–1.7B, Section 5.2, Figure 5) follows the Chinchilla protocol only to compare attention variants. Its only result is that DMA has the best perplexity at each scale. The paper fits no power law, reports no exponents and tests no extrapolation or allocation, so it uses scaling laws as an evaluation tool rather than testing them.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance: the authors conclude that DMA has the best perplexity across 80M–1.7B scales, beating the other attention variants. They also report better associative recall, large kernel speedups, better downstream scores at 1.7B and stronger needle-in-a-haystack extrapolation.
record.recipe_differences: This is a comparison of attention mechanisms trained at several model sizes, not a fit of language-model loss scaling laws or a compute-optimal allocation study.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched parameter scales (80M–1.7B) on SmolLMCorpus, the DMA attention variant has lower perplexity than MHA and NSA (Figure 5, text only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention-mechanism choice shifts the perplexity-vs-compute curve at fixed scale.

record.problems: The scaling comparison provides no numeric perplexity values in the text and no fitted power law or exponents. Its stated model-size range is 80M to 1.7B parameters, on one corpus.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream benchmark, associative-recall, kernel-speed, and needle-in-a-haystack results are not rows because they do not test the loss-scaling relationships or compute-optimal allocation in the claim.

untested.parts: No power-law fit or exponents; tokens, parameters and compute are not varied independently; perplexity values appear only in a figure.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger runs.
Chinchilla allocation is followed as a protocol, not tested.
Depth and width are not varied at fixed parameter count; attention variants differ by mechanism, not shape.
No other modality or training regime is tested.
Downstream scores come from a single 1.7B scale, with no relation to scale or loss.
No comparison of fitting choices or curve bending.

record.verdict_notes: The paper calls its variant comparison 'scaling laws', but it is an architecture benchmark. The study is not one of the original sources. The record's V1 limits_scope label is removed because the study does not test V1.

versions.untested_parts: The experiment compares parameter scales but does not fit a power law, report its exponents, independently vary training tokens or compute, or establish that the other factors are not bottlenecks.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The paper does not vary depth or width at a fixed parameter count to test architecture sensitivity.
No other modality or training regime is tested for the same power-law form.
Downstream scores are reported, but the paper does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
The paper does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices, nor test whether curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: DMA
rows.operation_detail: Compared perplexity across parameter scales on SmolLMCorpus.
rows.baseline: MHA, SWA, MLA, and NSA attention variants
rows.value: DMA maintains the best performance across various scales.
rows.note: The paper gives the comparative result in text, but reports no numeric perplexities or power-law fit. Figure 5 plots perplexity against FLOPs; its values are figure-only.
rows.check: The row records the study's own method compared with baselines (DMA vs MHA/SWA/MLA/NSA), not whether loss follows a power law in parameters, tokens or compute. No numeric perplexities or fit are given; values exist only in Figure 5. It should not be linked to V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported result is a relative perplexity comparison over the stated model-size range; it does not establish the power-law form or the separate token and compute relationships (r1).
